pr.title: Run the full gate once per head, in CI
pr.head: cc6b600e73cf0b481e6091736bcca45fd5432a40

summary: Projector's skills ask three parties to run a repository's full test suite on the same head. The author or fixer runs it before each push, CI runs it on the push, and the reviewer runs it again through project review gate. This pull request builds the gate-in-ci plan, so the suite runs once per head, in CI.
A new setting, review.gate_checks, names the GitHub Actions checks that run the suite, such as check. With it set, the parties split the work this way:

• The reviewer. project review gate waits up to 30 minutes for those checks on the exact head. It writes their result into the gate record that a local run already writes, so the incremental-review rule reads it unchanged.
  • The author and the fixer. implement and fix-pr run only the tests that cover their change and the review.gate command before a push.
  • The watch daemon. A new CHECKS event tells the fixer when a check fails on the head.

The gate exits 0 when every named check passed and 1 when one failed. It exits 75 when CI gives no evidence about the code: a check never ran, was cancelled or skipped, or timed out, or the head changed a file that decides what the check runs. On exit 75 the reviewer falls back to the full local gate on a trusted head, and to reading on an untrusted one. Reading CI runs nothing on the reviewer's machine, so an untrusted head gets CI's result too.

cards.title: What each gate exit means
cards.html:
ExitWhenThe reviewer
0Every named check concluded success, and the review.gate command passed or did not run.Treats the gate as passed.
1A named check concluded failure or timed_out.Treats it as a failing gate.
command's statusThe review.gate command failed, so CI is not read.Treats it as a failing gate.
75No evidence: a missing check, a timeout, a cancelled, skipped, neutral, stale, or action_required conclusion, a changed workflow file, or files that cannot be told.Runs the full gate locally on a trusted head, or reads an untrusted one.

cards.html:

groups.title: The setting and Projector's own opt-in
groups.kicker: A new review.gate_checks key, read by the gate command, and set for Projector itself
intro: review.gate_checks is a string of check names, separated by commas, in .projector.toml. With the key unset, nothing changes. review.gate keeps its meaning: a shell command the reviewer runs locally. With gate_checks set, that command covers only the part of the gate that CI cannot run.

Projector opts itself in. Its check job runs the Python suite, the site's lint and type check, and project check. Its new review.gate runs the plugin validations, the hooks tests, hooks/typecheck.sh, and git diff --check, which CI cannot run.

files.note: review gate reads both keys from the checkout's configuration, passes the parsed names to gate, and prints each check's conclusion and the reason for exit 75.

checks.text: The configuration comes from the operator's checkout, not from the head, so a head under review cannot change which checks vouch for it or which command runs.

files.note: Sets gate_checks = "check" and a review.gate for the steps CI cannot run.

checks.text: git diff --check "$2" HEAD compares the head with the merge base, because a plain git diff --check sees nothing in a clean scratch worktree.

groups.title: The gate waits for CI
groups.kicker: How project review gate reads the named checks, and when it refuses to trust them
intro: With names set, gate first runs the review.gate command, and only on a head that setup recorded as trusted. A failing command decides the gate with its own status. Otherwise await_checks polls every 20 seconds. Each poll reads each named check's latest run on the head with check_name=, one name at a time, and keeps only runs from the github-actions app.
A check gives no evidence, and the gate exits 75, in these cases:

• The head changed what the check runs. check_files asks GitHub which workflow file the run's check suite came from. It follows each local uses: ./ line to reusable workflows and local actions. A changed file in that set refuses CI, and so does a set that cannot be told.
  • No run is coming. While a named check has no run, coming lists the head's workflow runs. A run that is queued, in_progress, requested, waiting, or pending keeps the wait going. A run waiting for approval, every run finished, or no run after two minutes ends it.
  • No useful conclusion. The check concluded something other than success, failure, or timed_out, or it was still running after 30 minutes.

checks.text: Read-only calls against this pull request confirmed the response shapes the gate reads: check-runs?check_name=check returns this head's github-actions run, and actions/runs?check_suite_id= returns .github/workflows/check.yml as its path.

files.note: gate moves the trust check onto the command, and adds await_checks, ci_checks, coming, summarize_check, and check_files.

checks.text: Without names, an untrusted head is still refused before anything runs, as before. With names, an untrusted head skips the command and still reads CI.
incremental_rules refuses an untrusted head before it reads gate_passed, so a CI pass recorded on an untrusted head cannot carry an incremental review. Traced in incremental_rules.

For uses: ./, the form an action's own repository uses to test itself, target is empty and git ls-tree -- "" fails. gate then exits 1 with no record, which reads as a failing check, instead of exiting 75. A reproduction confirmed it. The review's thread asks to treat an empty target as the repository root.
A failed gh call during the 30-minute wait also ends gate with exit 1. The review lists exit 75 for that case as a suggestion.

files.note: A fake for the check-runs, workflow-runs, and check-suite endpoints, and CiGateTests, which covers each acceptance row of the plan's gate.

checks.text: The first and third subtests commit the same base and head. Within one second they get the same SHA, so setup finds the first subtest's lock and exits 1. That failure is what turned this head's check job red. Pinning the commit dates reproduces it every time. The review's thread asks for a distinct head per subtest.

groups.title: A CHECKS event for the fixer
groups.kicker: The watch daemon reports a failed check on the head to the fix role
intro: The watch daemon already reads each subscribed pull request's CI rollup, the combined state of its check runs and commit statuses, for the panel. Its query now also reads the first 20 contexts in the rollup, with GitHub's counts of check runs and statuses by state, which cover every context.

A failed context is a check run that concluded FAILURE, TIMED_OUT, or STARTUP_FAILURE, or a status in FAILURE or ERROR. projector/review, the status a changes-requested verdict posts, never counts. When the counts show more failures than the first page names, read_contexts reads later pages of 100 until it finds them or the pages end. The fix role then hears one CHECKS line per head, repeated after watch.renotify.

checks.text: The new query ran read-only against this pull request. It returned the counts and pageInfo, and failed_contexts named check, the job that failed on this head.

files.note: Adds the rollup contexts and the projector/review status to QUERY, adds CONTEXTS_QUERY for later pages, and emits CHECKS from route_fix.

checks.text: failure_count subtracts a failed projector/review status before the comparison, which was the plan review's last suggestion. test_a_failed_projector_review_status_reads_no_later_page_of_contexts covers it.
The event key is checks:<number>:<head>, so a new head starts silent until one of its own contexts fails.

files.note: The fake GitHub now pages rollup contexts and computes the counts by state. The tests cover once-per-head announcing, each failing and non-failing state, a failure on the second page, and the projector/review exclusion.

groups.title: The skills run less of the suite
groups.kicker: implement, fix-pr, finish, and review-pr follow the new setting
intro: Where review.gate_checks is set, implement and fix-pr run the tests for what changed and the review.gate command before a push, and each stack layer a rebase rewrites follows the same rule. fix-pr handles a CHECKS line. It reads the failing job's log, reproduces the failure, and fixes it, or reports a failure it cannot reproduce. finish accepts the named checks passing as the suite's evidence. review-pr runs gate on every head and says what to do on each exit.

files.note: Adds a paragraph on running gate with gate_checks and what exits 0, 1, and 75 mean.

checks.text: The exit 1 bullet says the review.gate command failing exits 1, but a failing command exits with its own status, as docs/cli.md says. The review lists the fix as a suggestion.

files.note: "Verify the current slice" and the stack rebase rule get the smaller gate.
Adds CHECKS as outstanding work and as an event, and gives step 2, the merge gate, and the stack layers the smaller gate.
Step 4 accepts the named checks passing on the head.
Says which part of the gate the check job runs, and that a push needs only the focused tests and the other steps.
